suggestion: Add a scheduled capture of the official injury report and the club depth pages on Wed, Thu, Fri and pre-kickoff, writing one immutable dated read per run with a hash.
problem_it_solves: A single capture cannot support backtesting, because a backtest needs the report as it was known before each kickoff, not as it reads today.
expected_impact: Turns the availability feature from a level into a series, which is what the no-lookahead rule requires.

suggestion: Point the capture harness at the official Game Book PDFs from a network that can reach static.www.nfl.com and store the parsed starting lineups and inactive lists.
problem_it_solves: The 'who actually started' side of the availability graph is empty for every fixture, which blocks the graph and every backtest built on it.
expected_impact: Fills the single largest gap in this desk and unlocks the expected-versus-actual comparison.

suggestion: Publish a per-club 'expected starter' table refreshed on every report publication, rather than a per-game table.
problem_it_solves: The per-game framing silently mixes captures taken at different times, which is exactly the lookahead the rules forbid.
expected_impact: Makes the time axis explicit and removes the need to argue about which capture a row came from.

suggestion: Flag depth rows that contradict an official transaction (IR placement, trade) automatically, on every capture.
problem_it_solves: Stale rows (Chargers' Henley, James and Pipkins; Patriots' Henderson) were found by hand this session and would otherwise reach the model.
expected_impact: Turns a manual audit into a permanent, cheap check.

suggestion: Keep the depth-string label attached to its source ('club chart, undated') and never present it as a measured depth.
problem_it_solves: The club charts are explicitly unofficial opinions; presenting them as measurements overstates them.
expected_impact: Removes the largest source of over-claiming in the desk.

suggestion: Record a 'surprise' column: the change in designation between consecutive reads, never the designation level alone.
problem_it_solves: A level (who is Out) is already priced in; only the change is information.
expected_impact: Matches the rule that the injury signal must be a surprise, not a level.

suggestion: Capture the club's own published inactives list for each fixture (for example the Patriots' 'Week 10 Inactives' page) into a separate table from the report.
problem_it_solves: The report has a Wednesday cut-off and misses players who are on IR; the club list is the game-day truth.
expected_impact: Gives the desk a game-day availability column without waiting for the Game Book pipeline.

suggestion: Publish the roster/IR sweep for the 28 clubs that played in Week 10 with an explicit status column per player, not a club-level flag.
problem_it_solves: 'Not listed' currently has two meanings (healthy, or on IR) and only one of them is correct.
expected_impact: Removes the ambiguity that the reserve-list requirement names.

suggestion: Reconcile the club abbreviation set (LAR, LA, AZ, JAX, LAR) into one published alias table with the official strings preserved verbatim.
problem_it_solves: Three official spellings of one club break joins between captures.
expected_impact: Small, permanent fix to a recurring data defect.

suggestion: Publish the Week 11 expectation table again, automatically, once the league publishes the Week 11 report, and diff it against this one.
problem_it_solves: The Week 11 report was not published at read time, so the current expectation table is built on the Week 10 report and is provisional.
expected_impact: Turns a provisional table into a dated one with a published delta.
